newsitem.title: USA: ABC unveils fall primetime TV lineup.
newsitem.headline: ABC unveils fall primetime TV lineup.

text.p: Walt Disney Co's ABC Television Network unit Monday unveiled its 1997-98 primetime schedule, adding five new 30-minute situation comedies and five one-hour dramas.

Among the changes announced by ABC was a new edition of the news program, "20/20" on Thursday nights at 2200 Eastern time, aimed at combating the ratings success of General Electric Co unit NBC's "Dateline" news program. NBC will air "Dateline" on three separate nights. ABC will also bring back "Wonderful World of Disney" Sundays at 1900 Eastern time as a lead-in to its "Sunday Night Movie."
Jamie Tarses, the new president of ABC Entertainment, was to formally introduce the new fall schedule to advertisers on Monday afternoon at Radio City Music Hall.
ABC is placing a heavy bet on one new series, "Timecop," a science fiction show set in the year 2007. It will air at 2000 ET, preceding "Monday Night Football."

Two 30-minute teen-oriented sitcoms, "Genie" about a divorced mother of two and a genie, and "Teen Angel," about a 15-year-old whose friend dies and comes back as his guardian angel, will air Fridays, beginning at 2100 ET.
"Dharma & Greg," about a free spirit daughter of hippie parents who marries the descendent of a family of blue bloods, airs Wednesdays at 2030 ET, between "Spin City" and "The Drew Carey Show."

On Tuesdays, with the departure of the hit, "Roseanne," "Home Improvement" moves from 2000 ET to 2100 ET. "Soul Man" takes over at 2000 ET and two new sitcoms will air: "Over the Top," with Tim Curry as an out-of-luck actor, airs at 2030 ET; "Hiller and Diller," about two TV comedy writers and written by real-life comedy writers Lowell Ganz and Babaloo Mandel, airs at 2130 ET.
